name: GePETO
fs_description: The GePETO project is a germanium refining recycling project in Belgium. It aims at strengthening Umicore's capabilities through technology development and facility upgrading. This will result in higher germanium recovery yields from existing feed, in innovative processes supporting the recovery of germanium out of complex waste streams from European industry and a more resilient supply of germanium products to the EU value chain.
fs_benefit: GePETO project will increase the security of the EU's supply for germanium, contributing to the achievements of the 2030 CRMA processing and recycling benchmarks. Umicore's facility in Belgium is one of the largest germanium refining and recycling operations in the world. It holds a systemic position in ensuring the supply of germanium products to the European value chains. These germanium products are indispensable to the production of various strategically important and high growth applications, such as optical fiber cables, high efficient solar cells for space satellites and space exploration, various micro-electronics applications and infra-red night vision systems. O European Union, 2025

name: ReGAIN
fs_description: The ReGAlN project is a substitution project, focusing on the expansion and transformation of Umicore's Ge wafering facility located in Olen, Belgium. This project entails the industrialization of a new technology supporting the re-use of germanium substrates. These thin film germanium substrates are serving the space solar cell and industry. These innovative micro-electronics substrates allow the industry to significantly reduce its consumption of germanium, enabling the required growth of the end markets like space power.
fs_benefit: This project will contribute to the security of the EU's supply of strategic raw materials by substituting a substantial amount of germanium through the use of thin film germanium substrates. This increases the capability of the EU to produce affordable, flexible and lightweight solar cells, which is crucial for European non-dependence and competitiveness in the field of space solar power generation. Furthermore, this project will produce substrates that are re-usable and come with a lower environmental footprint. O European Union, 2025

name: Chvaletice manganese Project
fs_description: The Chvaletice Manganese Project is an integrated extraction and processing project located in the Czech Republic. The project involves the development of a tailings extraction section and a high-purity refining section to re-process a readily leachable manganese deposit hosted in the tailings of a decommissioned mine. The project's goal is to produce battery grade high-purity manganese products, principally for use in the cathode of lithium-ion batteries in the EU market.
fs_benefit: The Chvaletice Manganese project will reduce Europe's reliance on imports of raw battery materials by providing a secure, local source of up to 20% of projected 2030 European demand for high-purity manganese, according to the promoter. As a source of an important battery raw material, the Project is well positioned to support the EU and the Czech Republic's green goals of reducing the region's carbon footprint via the energy transition and working towards a more sustainable, circular economy. The project will create full-time jobs, tax revenues and numerous commercial opportunities for Czech businesses creating a multiplier effect in the region. O European Union, 2025

name: Cínovec lithium project
fs_unfc: Extraction E2 // F2.1 // G1+G2 and G1+G2+G3 Processing Q // F2.1 //
fs_description: Cinovec lithium project is an integrated extraction and processing project located approximately 105 km north-west of Prague, in the historical CinovecZinnwald mining district (Czech Republic). The project aims to extract Zinnwaldite - a lithium bearing mineral - from an underground mine, concentrate the lithium ore and produce battery grade lithium carbonate via chemical processing. The project plans to use renewable energy (solar) for its energy intensive operations.
fs_benefit: According to project promoter, Cinovec lithium integrated project will be able to annually produce 7-8% of the projected 2030 European lithium demand, with the estimated start of production in 2028. This would make a meaningful contribution to the security of the EU's supply of lithium and to the achievements of the 2030 CRMA benchmarks. The promoter intends to directly supply the European market for production of electric vehicle (EV) batteries. The new location of the processing plant - brownfield area provides additional positive environmental and social effects regarding new jobs where traditional coal-based power stations are about to be laid down. O European Union, 2025

name: CO2 Graphite
fs_description: C02GRAPHlTE project is a processing project located in Estonia. It aims to build a large-scale facility to produce battery-grade graphite based on the synthesis of carbon materials from carbon dioxide (C02). This technology is the result of R&D efforts started over 10 years ago in the University of Tartu (Estonia).
fs_benefit: C02GRAPHlTE project would make a meaningful contribution to the security of the EU's supply, contributing to the achievement of the 2030 benchmarks. The use of carbon-negative technology allows the project promoter to capture and convert industrial C02 emissions into batterygrade graphite. This project involves partnerships with various entities across the EU, as well as suppliers and off takers. O European Union, 2025

name: Sakatti Project
materials: cobalt, platinum group metals, copper, nickel (battery grade)
fs_materials: Copper, Platinum group metals, battery grade Nickel and Cobalt
fs_unfc: Extraction: E1.2 // F2.1 // G 1+2 Processing: E1.2 // F2.1 // G 1+2
fs_description: The Sakatti project by Anglo American is an innovative mining project in northern Finland focused on extracting high-grade strategic raw materials including copper, nickel, platinum group metals and cobalt. Sakatti is being designed and developed as a highly automated, low-carbon underground operation, with minimal surface footprint while providing a secure and stable source of strategic raw materials crucial for the energy and digital transitions. Sakatti expected to deliver around 100,000 tonnes of copperequivalent metal, enough for 1.3 million electric vehicles.
fs_benefit: The Sakatti project is strategically important for the EU as it bolsters the extraction and processing capacities for strategic raw materials needed in the energy and digital sectors. It enhances supply security and reduces reliance on non-EU sources, aligning with the EU's goals for resilience and sustainable resource access under the Critical Raw Materials Act. Sakatti's metals are likely to be converted locally in the EU into products such as Precursor Cathode Active Material (PCAM) and Cathode Active Material (CAM), which are feed materials to produce EV batteries in multiple EU states, for the destination of EU consumers. O European Union, 2025

name: KELIBER LITHIUM PROJECT
fs_unfc: Extraction: E1.2 // F1.2 // G2 Processing: E1.2 // F1.2 // G2
fs_description: Sibanye-Stillwater's Keliber Lithium Project is a project for integrated lithium extraction and processing in Finland. It aims to develop a sustainable operation to produce battery-grade lithium hydroxide (LiOH). The mining operations and the processing plant are located in Kaustinen and Kokkola, in Central Ostrobothnia, Finland, which holds some of the most significant lithium deposits in Europe. The production process is composed of three stages: mining and production of an ore concentrate in the Kaustinen area, and LiOH production at the refinery in the Kokkola Industrial Park.
fs_benefit: The Keliber project would make a meaningful contribution to the security of the EU's supply of lithium and to the achievements of the 2030 CRMA benchmarks. According to the promoter, the project has the potential to cover 2-5% of projected 2030 European demand for lithium. Keliber will supply the European market for production of batteries and the electric vehicle (EV) value chain, whose transition to electric cars would otherwise be entirely sourced outside EU. O European Union, 2025

name: Kolmisoppi
fs_description: The Kolmisoppi extraction project by Terrafame Ltd in Finland, targeting the exploitation of its substantial nickel and cobalt resources starting in 2028. This initiative aims to extend Terrafame's nickel and cobalt operational capabilities and supporting its integrated battery chemicals plant. The Kolmisoppi project is set to sustain and enhance the production of strategic materials utilizing bioleaching technology that reduces energy consumption and carbon emissions.
fs_benefit: The Kolmisoppi extraction project will support the European Union's goals of securing strategic raw materials nickel and cobalt and building a sustainable battery value chain. This project will ensure the continued operation of Terrafame, which is essential for the EU to reach its 2030 CRMA benchmark for Battery Grade Nickel and ensure sustainable production until 2051. The whole potential of Kolmisoppi enables operations to continue even into the 2080s, if metal prices develop positively in the coming decades. O European Union, 2025

name: Project Fortum Hydromet
materials: lithium (battery grade), copper, nickel (battery grade), cobalt
fs_description: Project Fortum Hydromet is a black mass recycling project in Finland. The project is a planned extension of an existing hydrometallurgical plant producing nickel, cobalt, lithium (battery grade) and copper. The company aims to have the first stage of the expansion operational by 2029, and the fullsized plant is estimated to start in 2032. The new plant is planned to be built in the adjacent land area of the existing plant. The plant will use black mass and pCAM/CAM production waste as its feedstock.
fs_benefit: Project Fortum Hydromet would make a meaningful contribution to the security of the EU's supply of nickel, cobalt, lithium and copper, contributing to the achievement of the 2030 recycling benchmarks. It would add black mass and pCAM/CAM recycling capacity in Europe and increasing the production of fully separated, battery-grade metals, namely nickel, cobalt and lithium hydroxide. The plant would also produce graphite and copper. When reaching its maximum production, the project would cover approximately 2.4% of nickel, 2.6% of cobalt, and 1.7% of lithium demand for e-mobility in the EU. Off-takers are located in more than one Member State and the project has wider benefits for downstream users. O European Union, 2025

name: Hycamite TCD Technologies Ltd
fs_description: The Hycamite TCD Technologies project is a processing project in Kokkola, Finland. It produces clean hydrogen and solid, high-value carbon products by splitting methane. Through its proprietary catalysts, Hycamite can tailor its carbon products according to customer requirements into, e.g., battery-grade graphite." It is at the construction stage of an industrial-scale demonstration plant at the Kokkola Industrial Park for producing battery-grade graphite using an innovative methane-splitting technology. The project promoter has been operating a pilot plant for approximately 3 years and is further de-risking the process through the construction of a commercial demonstration plant.
fs_benefit: Hycamite TCD Technologies project is strategically important for the European Union as it directly addresses the critical need for graphite. which plays an essential role in producing anodes for lithiumion batteries, which are key components in electric vehicles (EVs) and stationary energy storage systems. According to the promoter, the project could capture up to 40% of the European market for battery-grade graphite, contributing substantially to meeting the EU rising demand for the decarbonization of the transport and energy sectors. O European Union, 2025

name: Jervois Finland Cobalt Refinery Expansion Project
fs_description: The Jervois Finland Cobalt is a processing project in the Kokkola Industrial Park in Finland. It aims to establish a new, state-of-the-art cobalt refinery to produce battery grade cobalt sulphate. The project promoter has deep technological expertise specific to cobalt refining, having manufactured advanced cobalt products at its cobalt refinery facility in Kokkola since 1968. The refinery will leverage existing infrastructure at the Kokkola Industrial Park, which provides necessary utilities and sbpports streamlined operations, contributing to its technical readiness.
fs_benefit: The Jervois Finland Cobalt project is set to make a meaningful contribution to the security of the EU's supply by increasing its refined cobalt production capacity by over 20%, according to project promoter. This expansion is important to meet the rising demand for battery grade cobalt, essential for electric vehicle batteries, and help ensure the EU's strategic autonomy in critical raw materials. The sourcing strategy for the feedstock raw materials further strengthens the region's supply resilience by diversifying its input sources and adding recycling capacity. O European Union, 2025

name: CAREMAG
materials: rare earth elements for permanent magnets, boron (metallurgy grade)
fs_description: CAREMAG is a processing project located in France. It aims at creating an environmentally friendly production unit for pure rare earth oxides (Neodymium, Praseodymium, Terbium, Dysprosium) from permanent magnets to be recycled from production scrap (magnet manufacturing, turbine and motor assembly plants) and end-of-life equipment as well as from rareearth concentrates from mines. The processing plant will be built in an existing industrial area, limiting the potential negative environmental impacts. It will make use of the best available technologies for a reduced environmental impact in terms of C02, water use and energy consumption.
fs_benefit: CAREMAG processing project has the potential to cover more than 500/00/0 of heavy rare earths needs and up to 3% of light rare earth needs in terms of European needs by 2030, according to project promoter. This would make a meaningful contribution to the security of the EU's supply of rare earths for magnets reducing the current dependency in third countries and contributing to build a permanent magnets ecosystem in the EU. O European Union, 2025

name: Emili
fs_unfc: Extraction Q // F2.1 // G1+G2 and G1+G2+G3 Processing Q // F2.1 // G2
fs_description: EMILI is an integrated hard-rock lithium extraction and processing project located in France. The upstream project encompasses an underground mine and a concentration plant to produce a mica concentrate from Beauvoir deposit 40 km away, the EMILI project also aims at constructing a lithium refinery, able to produce battery grade lithium hydroxide monohydrate (LHM) using mica ore concentrate as the source of lithium. The project, which will benefit from an operating quarry activity and an existing industrial area, will adhere to IRMA international certification scheme, focusing on minimising environmental impact, maximising resource efficiency and social impact
fs_benefit: EMILI project would annually produce battery grade lithium hydroxide monohydrate (LHM) covering 5% of the EU demand in 2030, according to the project promoter. The estimated start of production by 2029, would allow EMILI project making a meaningful contribution to the security of the EU's supply of lithium and contribute to the achievements of the 2030 CRMA benchmarks. O European Union, 2025

name: BAM4EVER (Phase I&II)
fs_description: The BAM4EVER project is a processing project located in France. It aims to establish a graphite Battery Anode Material (BAM) production facility to supply European battery gigafactories. The equipment needed for all steps of production is already in place and currently producing at smaller scale. Tokai COBEX Savoie, French subsidiary of a Japanese company is developing an expansion project for industrialising high-performance artificial Graphite BAM that will be 20 times less C02 intensive compared to existing producers and technologies.
fs_benefit: BAM4EVER project is considered strategic due to its potential to supply approximately 10% of EU demand for battery grade graphite, according to the promoter. The project will allow for reducing the dependency from China, which currently controls over 95% of global supplies for both natural and artificial graphite-based BAM. The project will also significantly contribute to the target of the Critical Raw Materials Act of increasing the EU processing capacity to source at least 40% of the EU's annual consumption. O European Union, 2025

name: MagFactory
materials: rare earth elements for permanent magnets
fs_materials: Rare Earth Elements for Magnets (Nd, Pr, Tb, Dy, Gd, sm, and ce)
fs_description: The MagFactory project is a recycling project In France. It aims to establish a cutting-edge production facility for rare earth magnets in Europe. Vertically integrated, the project utilizes a costeffective circular model, from recycling magnet scraps to re-manufacturing new rare earths permanent magnets. The processes involved have been developed by R&D and have been tested at the laboratory and pilot plant levels by the promoters.
fs_benefit: The MagFactory project would establish a Net Zero magnet production facility in Europe, addressing strategically important markets such as renewable energy. According to project promoter, production in 2029 would represent 1.25 % of the total expected demand and 5 % of the amount targeted for recycling. Moreover, production could double in 2031 thanks to the start of production of a new manufacturing line in the plant. The project aims to reduce EU dependence on raw materials for rare earth element permanent magnets from third countries, improve environmental sustainability by significantly cutting the carbon footprint of rare earth permanent magnets, and enhance industrial resilience. O European Union, 2025

name: GALLICAM
materials: nickel (battery grade), cobalt, lithium (battery grade), graphite (battery grade), manganese (battery grade), copper
fs_description: Sibanye-Stillwater's GalliCam project is a processing project near Le Havre in France. It aims at reconverting the existing Sandouville nickel refinery capacity to be able to produce precursor of Cathode Active Materials (pCAM) containing nickel, manganese, and cobalt (NMC). The project is based on a disruptive direct pCAM production process using hydrochloric acid as primary refining medium from Mixed Hydroxide Precipitate (MHP - produced from mines). The process is designed so that it can also use Black Mass (BM - sourced from end-of-life or scrapped batteries) as a feed. The project will be implemented on the Sandouville brownfield site, eliminating the need for artificialisation of new land and reducing its impact on biodiversity.
fs_benefit: The GalliCam project would make a meaningful contribution to the security of the EU's supply for precursors of NMC Cathode Active Materials composed, contributing to the achievements of the CRMA 2030 objectives for processing. The project will be key for developing a competitive and resilient European Lithium-ion batteries value chain. Developing a EU production for pCAM to support the growth in the EV market will be a major challenge towards the shift to a more sustainable and environmentally friendly mobility. O European Union, 2025

name: Hydrometallurgy
materials: lithium (battery grade), cobalt, nickel (battery grade), manganese (battery grade), graphite (battery grade)
fs_materials: Cobalt, Nickel, Manganese and Lithium (battery grade)
fs_description: The HYDRO-BATTERY project aims to develop an innovative, effcient and competitive solution for the recycling of electric vehicle batteries or battery production waste (production scraps and end of life batteries), located in Dunkirk, Hauts-de-France region (France). The technology allows recovery of critical raw materials contained in the black mass from battery pretreatment. These obtained materials such as nickel, cobalt, manganese and lithium are of battery quality and can thus be reintroduced into new battery manufacturing. Based on processes mastered by Orano, this technology is distinguished by its economical use of chemical reagents and electrical equipment exclusively allowing to benefit from a highly decarbonized energy available in France.
fs_benefit: By enabling recycling at battery purity levels, this technology helps improve the sustainability and circularity of critical raw materials in the EU market. It also allows the development of a strategic and autonomous supply of the emerging European battery industry. This new technology will enable European battery players to keep control over their materials while meeting the recycling content reintegration targets set by EU battery regulations while promoting the development of the circular economy. Recycling offers urban mining ressources which contributes to reinforce the European sovereignty. O European Union, 2025

name: Ageli
fs_description: Ageli is one of the world's most sustainable integrated lithium extraction and processing project, located in France's Alsace region lead by Eramet, EU leader in lithium production and ÉS, world expert in geothermal energy. It aims to extract lithium from geothermal brine to produce battery-grade lithium carbonate. The promoter's intention is to industrialise a sustainable process that combines geothermal energy and lithium production with a low carbon footprint. As an output, Ageli will contribute to supporting the expansion of the EU battery industry over the long term, as it is a key precursor for Lithium-ion batteries used for electric mobility or stationary storage on mainland Europe.
fs_benefit: The Ageli project covers the extraction and purification stages within the lithium supply chain, contributing to the creation of a secure and resilient European battery ecosystem. The aim of the Ageli project is intrinsically aligned with European objectives set out in the Critical Raw Materials Act and supports the EU's ambition to secure a sustainable energy transition. In addition to contributing to European sovereignty in critical metals, Ageli also intends to introduce low-carbon lithium production and reduce greenhouse gas emissions compared to the conventional production of battery-grade lithium. O European Union, 2025

name: Viridian Lithium
fs_description: The Viridian Lithium project is a lithium processing project located in France. The project will operate primarily as a service company to convert various grades of lithium carbonate to refined batterygrade lithium hydroxide monohydrate. This independent lithium refinery aims to provide for the conversion and purification of lithium salts used as cathode precursors for the manufacturing of lithium-ion batteries for Electric Vehicles (EV).
fs_benefit: This project aims to help bridge the gap in Europe's supply chain of lithium battery materials, thus strengthening the European EV value chain. According to the promoter, this project will account for approximately 10% of the projected battery grade lithium hydroxide demand by 2030. By doing so, the project will contribute to the ambitions of the EU regarding the processing of critical raw materials, as set out in the Critical Raw Materials Act. Furthermore, this project has the potential to indirectly assist the EU's ambition for lithium recycling through the intellectual property developed by the promoter for processes designed to refine various lithium materials, which potentially will be produced by battery recycling customers. O European Union, 2025

name: European Initiative for Strategic and Sustainable Graphite Production
fs_title: European Initiative for Strategic and Sustainable
fs_name: European Initiative for Strategic and Sustainable Graphite
fs_description: The project European Initiative for Strategic and Sustainable Graphite Production is developing a processing plant in northern France. The project will utilize natural graphite sourced from Northern Graphite's Okanjande mine in Namibia as the input material, to be transformed into high-purity graphite concentrate into battery anode material ("BAM").
fs_benefit: The project European Initiative for Strategic and Sustainable Graphite Production will contribute to the EU's supply of battery grade graphite by establishing a new plant for transforming graphite into Battery Anode Material with the potential to cover about 4% of the European demand. The planned activities are committed to environmental, social, and governance principles, ensuring all project activities align with global best practices, also aiming to generate socio-economic benefits to the local economy both in the EU and Namibia. O European Union, 2025

name: Zero Carbon Lithium
fs_description: Vulcan is building the world's first carbon neutral, integrated lithium and renewable energy business to decarbonise battery production. Vulcan's Lionheart Project, located in the Upper Rhine Valley Brine Field bordering Germany and France, is the largest lithium resource in Europe and a tier-one lithium project globally. Harnessing natural heat to produce lithium from sub-surface brines and to power conversion to battery-quality material and using its in-house industry-leading Adsorption-Type Direct Lithium Extraction technology VULSORB@, Vulcan is building a local, low-cost source of sustainable lithium for European electric vehicle batteries.
fs_benefit: This project will play a crucial role in securing a sustainable lithium supply within the EU, enabling the production of battery-quality lithium chemicals from a domestically sourced mineral resource. With a potential operational lifespan exceeding 30 years, it is poised to generate substantial local employment opportunities. Furthermore, the project offers significant crossborder benefits beyond the host Member State, supported by established offtake agreements with leading European and global downstream industries. O European Union, 2025

name: ProHiPerSi
fs_description: ProHiPerSi is a substitution project in Germany. It addresses the increase in performance of lithiumion batteries while at the same time reducing the specific production costs through a novel siliconbased anode active material (AAM). The material has been proven to significantly increase both the energy density and the fast-charge capability of state-of-the-art lithium-ion batteries. The AAM has been designed in a way that allows for its gradual implementation into already existing cell production lines as a replacement for graphite.
fs_benefit: ProHiPerSi project would make a meaningful contribution to the security of the EU's supply of strategic raw materials by substituting a batterygrade graphite by means of an alternative siliconbased anode active material. This material promises substantial performance enhancements in terms of faster charging capabilities, reduced carbon footprint and increased energy density. O European Union, 2025

name: Lithium Hydroxide Converter Guben
fs_description: The Lithium Hydroxide Converter Guben processing project by Rock Tech Guben GmbH is set to develop a conversion plant in Guben, Germany designed to process the lithium bearing ore spodumene into high-quality, battery-grade lithium hydroxide monohydrate (LHM) to serve the European markets. Apart from processing primary lithium, the plant will also refine lithium recyclates from recycling, contributing to a closed-loop lithium value chain in the EU.
fs_benefit: The Lithium Hydroxide Convertor Guben (LHCG) project will enhance the EU processing capacities for lithium and strengthen the domestic supply chain for strategic raw materials, particularly within the battery sector. By focusing on local production of battery-grade lithium hydroxide monohydrate, the project is supporting the growing demand for electric vehicles. The establishment of a robust self-sufficient supply chain also reduces the EU's dependency on non-EU suppliers and enhances supply chain security and resilience. O European Union, 2025

name: Metlen BAUX-EU, GALLANT, LEADER
promoter: Metlen Energy and Metals and European Bauxites
fs_description: The BAUX-EU, GALLANT and LEADER projects form an integrated extraction and processing project located in Greece. This project aims to develop an integrated production line for three critical and strategic raw materials in the EU, namely bauxite, gallium and alumina. This project entails an initiative aimed at developing a green extraction line for bauxite, with a main output of alumina, next to additional gallium extraction. Next to this, the project will also develop a new alumina production line, as well as focus on the processing of gallium
fs_benefit: These projects support the EU's strategy to secure a reliable, domestically sourced supply of multiple strategic raw materials, reducing dependency on third countries. Furthermore, this integrated project demonstrates a high level of innovation, as artificial intelligence will be applied during extraction activities. These projects also entail a significantly reduced environmental impact due to the high level of electrification both during extraction and processing activities. O European Union, 2025

name: RECOVER-IT
materials: copper, nickel (battery grade), platinum group metals
fs_materials: Copper, Nickel (battery grade), Platinum Group Metals
fs_description: Resources Extraction and Circular Optimization Via Effluent Recovery in Italy RECOVER-IT - is a recycling project in Italy promoted by Circular Materials. It aims to recover strategic raw materials trapped in industrial wastewater through the company's proprietary low carbon intensity SRMs extraction process, including nickel, copper and platinum group metals (PGMs). The Project is already operating from Circular Materials Hub Zero "CMHO" in Cadoneghe (PD) and will reach maximum throughput in Italy by 2029. As capacity for each CMH grows, the company will expand its intake of SRM-rich waste to other sources already successfully tested by the company, including electronic waste and black mass derived from endof-life batteries.
fs_benefit: RECOVER-IT would make a meaningful contribution to the security of the EU's supply of strategic raw materials by recycling nickel, copper, and PGMs from industrial wastewater while reducing the environmental footprint of industrial processes. According to project promoter, RECOVER-IT would redirect almost 30% of non-ferrous metal recovery volume from the plating sector in Italy back into the value chain. After the successful implementation of RECOVER-IT, the company plans to begin international production activities in wholly owned hubs across different Member States in EU. O European Union, 2025

name: Alpha Project
fs_description: Alpha - Recycling project is a recycling project located in Rosignano Solvay (Italy). It aims to establish an in-house palladium (Pd) recovery and catalyst production This initiative is a major step towards 100% circularity for palladium, a critical raw material used for the production of hydrogen peroxide. This project will not only enhance competitiveness and operational efficiency but also contribute to the EU's goal of securing critical raw material supply chains.
fs_benefit: Alpha -Recycling project would make a meaningful contribution to the security of the EU's supply of palladium, a platinum group metal, contributing to the achievement of the 2030 recycling benchmark. Palladium is used in several relevant technologies and sectors such as catalytic converters from internal combustion vehicles and those used in electrolysers for obtaining hydrogen fuel. Palladium is also used to produce hydrogen peroxide, which is widely used in the semiconductor industry as a washing solution for the manufacturing of chips. O European Union, 2025

name: LIFE-22-ENV- IT- INSPIREE
materials: rare earth elements for permanent magnets
fs_description: LIFE22-ENV-lT-lNSPlREE is a recycling project in the province of Frosinone, Italy. It aims for the recovery of Rare Earths from NdFeB permanent magnets extracted from hard disks and electric motors. In a two-level process, permanent magnets will first be disassembled (level l), after which REE will be recovered via hydrometallurgy (level II). The output materials of this process will be REE oxides, oxalates, carbonates, and other salts. The Rare Earth Recovery Facility is designed to utilize existing infrastructure of the industrial site.
fs_benefit: The project aims to develop and implement circular economy routes for REES by considering WEEE and end-of-life electric vehicles as sources of raw materials. This approach aligns with the goal of increasing the recycling rates of critical raw materials, thus ensuring a more resilient supply chain for these strategic materials, and contributing to the 25% recycling capacity goal established by the EU. By recycling REES within the EU, the project aims to reduce dependency on imports from nonEU countries. This contributes to building a more resilient supply chain, which is a key benchmark for 2030. O European Union, 2025

name: Portovesme CRM Hub
materials: lithium (battery grade), nickel (battery grade), cobalt, copper
fs_description: The Portovesme CRM Hub is a recycling project in Portovesme, Sardinia, Italy. It aims to use advanced hydrometallurgical technologies to recover critical raw materials from black mass generated by the pre-treatment of end-of-life batteries and scraps sourced across Europe. The facility will convert black mass into Mixed Hydroxide Precipitate (MHP) product containing nickel, cobalt and copper, as well as production of lithium carbonate. It strategically bridges the gap by building and operating a black mass treatment facility, using advanced technology with high recoveries rates of critical materials, managing battery chemistry variations and reducing risks and costs.
fs_benefit: The Portovesme CRM Hub would contribute to the EU's supply of strategic raw materials by recovering critical materials (lithium, nickel, cobalt, copper) through highly efficient battery recycling, aiming a recovery rate reaching 95%. This project would directly support the CRMA goal of recycling at least 25% of the EU's annual consumption of these materials by 2030. The project be sourcing black mass from various shredders across the EU, including European OEMs, battery gigafactories and waste collectors. The resulting products will be distributed within the EU market. O European Union, 2025

name: Pulawy Rare Earths Separation Plant
materials: rare earth elements for permanent magnets
fs_materials: Rare Earth Elements for Magnets (Nd, Pr, Tb, Dy, Gd, Sm, and Ce)
fs_description: T e Pulawy Rare Earths Separation Plant project is set to establish a rare earth elements (REES) separation plant in Pulawy, Poland, dedicated to processing mixed rare earth carbonates into essential oxides such as Neodymium, Praseodymium, and also a heavy rare earth concentrate.
fs_benefit: The Pulawy Rare Earths Separation Plant processing project aligns with the European Union's objectives to bolster domestic processing capabilities by increasing independence in strategic rare earth elements (REES) and thereby decreasing reliance on non-EU suppliers. According to project promoter, it is expected to contribute substantially to the EU's goal of 40% self-reliance in critical raw material processing by 2030. The plant targets ahnual production of 1,018t NdPr Oxide alongside; 805t separated Nd Oxide, and 212t separated Pr qxide. A heavy rare earth carbonateproduct will also be produced. By supporting the development of a resilient supply chain, the project facilitates downstream manufacturing processes for rare earth element permanent magnets and other high-tech products, which are crucial for the supply of strategic technologies such as electric vehicles and wind tilirbines. O European Union, 2025

name: POLVOLT
promoter: Elemental Battery Metals Sp. z o.o.
materials: nickel (battery grade), copper, cobalt, lithium (battery grade), platinum group metals, manganese (battery grade)
fs_description: POLVOLT is a recycling project in Poland. It focuses on the establishment of a large-scale facility dedicated to the recovery and recycling of critical raw materials crucial for the development of electromobility and renewable energy technologies. Specifically, the facility will focus on the production of chemical compounds of battery metals such as nickel, cobalt, manganese and lithium. The materials will be derived from black mass recovered from spent batteries and production waste from battery manufacturing facilities. The facility will also produce Grade A electrolytic copper, which is vital to produce copper foil used in lithium-ion battery anodes. Platinum Group Metals will be recovered from e-scrap delivered to the plant by extensive Elemental's collection network.
fs_benefit: The POLVOLT Project is a pioneering initiative that represents a significant advancement in sustainable industrial practices, with a strong emphasis on circular economy principles and the strategic goals outlined in the CRM Act. According to project promoter, the plant will be the largest facility of this kind in Europe and will produce the raw materials enabling 450.000 2.ooo.ooo electric cars to be built annually. O European Union, 2025

name: Romano Mine
fs_description: The Romano Mine project is a lithium extraction project located in Portugal It aims to mine lithium bearing minerals through both open-pit and underground mining using standard mining technologyq The output of this project would contribute to the production of lithium hydroxide monohydrate, used in both the lithium-ion battery and energy storage industries.
fs_benefit: The Romano Mine would contribute to the EU 's domestic extraction capacity of lithium, a raw material essential for the energy transition. According to the project promoter the extraction project would be covering between 41 and 56% of the 10% annual EU lithium consumption benchmark by 2030 in a low and high demand scenario. By doing so, the project would reduce the dependency of the EU on this critical raw material, aligning with the objectives set out in the Critical Raw Materials Act. The project would also create direct and indirect employment opportunities for local and regional residents. O European Union, 2025

name: Barroso Lithium Project
fs_description: The Barroso Lithium Project is an extraction project located in Northern Portugal. It aims to produce battery grade spodumene concentrate, ceramic feldspar/quartz, and low-grade bulk pegmatite. The project will apply conventional production techniques, amplify positive social impact in the region, while minimising environmental impact, visual disturbance and carbon footprint. The Project Promoter is owned by the listed company, Savannah Resources PLC, which means any EU investor can take part in the future success of the venture.
fs_benefit: The Barroso Lithium Project would make a meaningful contribution to the secure supply of lithium. The Project promoter expects the operation to supply enough lithium for 32 GWh of battery manufacturing per year, the equivalent of at least half a million fully electric cars annually. Hence, the Project could supply as much as 10% of the EU's EV related lithium demand by 2030. This project will position Portugal as a key player in the EU's battery raw materials value chain, potentially leading to the development of downstream industries in the country, while providing feedstock for other EU players. name: Lift One
fs_description: The Lift One project by Lifthium Energy, S.A., aims to establish a lithium refining plant in Portugal, contributing to the EU's capacity for lithium processing. By employing pioneering electrolysis technology primarily powered by renewable energy, the plant will transform lithium into battery-grade lithium hydroxide, essential for electric vehicle batteries. The integration of recycled materials, such as lithium from end-of-life batteries, emphasizes circular economy principles, reducing environmental impact and reliance on natural resource extraction.
fs_benefit: The Lift One processing project bolsters the European Union's ambitions for industrial and technological leadership by enhancing capacity for lithium hydroxide production, essential for electric mobility and renewable energy storage sectors. By reducing reliance on non-EU imports of battery grade lithium and strengthen EU's supply chain this will also supply the raw materials to a more resilient EU battery supply chain. name: SALROM Baia de Fier
fs_description: The SALROM Baia de Fier project is an extraction project, situated in the mineral-rich region of Baia de Fier in Romania. This project has the objective to re-open a historic mine and extract graphitebearing schists to produce high-quality graphite, using advanced techniques designed to minimize material losses and reduce environmental impact. The output of this extraction will be tailored for battery production, particularly for electric vehicles (EVs) and energy storage systems.
fs_benefit: The SALROM Baia de Fier project would help developing a sustainable and secure source of battery-grade graphite in the EU, thereby reducing reliance on imports and supporting the increasing demand in the clean energy and digital technology sectors. As such, the project enhances the strategic autonomy of the EU and supports the transition to a sustainable and circular economy, aligning with the objectives of the Critical Raw Materials Act and the European Green Deal. Furthermore, according to the promoter this project will generate employment, and support the local economy. O European Union, 2025

name: Rovina
fs_description: The Rovina project is a gold-copper extraction project located in Romania. The aim of this project is to produce high-grade copper concentrate from three Cu-Au porphyry style deposits in close proximity. The mining will take place over a period of 35 years from two open pits and one underground mine, with an estimated starting date in 2027.
fs_benefit: The Rovina project would contribute directly to the supply of copper in the EU, contributing to the security of this critical mineral and the strategic autonomy of the EU. According to the project promoter, Rovina copper production would represent between 2.4 and 4.6 % of the EU forecasted demand by 2030. As such, the project would align with the objectives of the EU, set out in the Critical Raw Materials Act. Furthermore, it is estimated that the project would generate employment and have positive impacts for both the local and regional economy. O European Union, 2025

name: Verde Magnesium
fs_description: The Verde Magnesium project is an extraction project located in Romania. This project implies the extraction of magnesium ores by restarting mining activities from one of the world's biggest deposits of brucite ore. These ores will become feedstock for a magnesium smelter to be built, which is still to be further developed. As an extraction project, it sits at the foundation of the metallic magnesium value chain, providing a strategic raw material valuable across different EU industries. The business model adopts the principles of circular economy: clean technology to produce low-carbon magnesium, use waste streams generated by various industries in the magnesium production process, generation of low-carbon by-products to serve as raw materials for other industries.
fs_benefit: This extraction project holds strategic importance for the EU as it contributes to its extraction capacity by providing both a rapid and long-term reliable feedstock solution of magnesium ore production. Given the EU's current non-existing primary magnesium production, this project would significantly contribute to achieving the 2030 extraction and processing benchmarks. According to the promoter, once the smelter is built, it would be able meet 5-10% of the EU's medium-term magnesium demand and 30—40% in the long term, aligning with the CRM Act's processing benchmarks. name: MINA DOADE PROJECT
fs_description: The Mina Doade Project is an extraction project in the Northwest of Spain, within the region of Galicia. The project addresses exploitation of pegmatite, a lithium bearing ore, through underground mining and a mineral processing plant for concentration. The project will use well-proven mining and beneficiation technologies to develop a small-scale underground mining operation, which will reduce dust and noise emissions as well as the impacts on the local ecosystem. The use of ore processing waste (tailings) to backfill underground mined cavities will significantly reduce the need for surface storage of mining waste and ore processing tailings.
fs_benefit: The Mina Doade Project has a clear potential to meaningfully contribute to the security of the EU's supply of lithium and to the achievements of the 2030 CRMA benchmarks. The project is focused on achieving the first two steps of this value chain for this Strategic Raw Material and currently already has a pre-agreement for the supply of lithium concentrates obtained with an European company that need this raw material to obtain lithium products downstream of the aforementioned value chain. name: LAS NAVAS
fs_description: LAS NAVAS project is an extraction project close to Cåceres, Spain. It aims to extract lithium bearing minerals and to produce battery-grade lithium hydroxide in the long term. The lithium mineralization of the Las Navas deposit is primarily composed of spodumene, amblygonite, and lithium micas, mainly lepidolite and zinnwaldite. Other economically significant minerals present include cassiterite and columbo-tantalite. The technology needed to extract the ore, which is widely available and used in producing spodumene mines in Australia and Canada, would be made available by EU providers.
fs_benefit: LAS NAVAS project would make a meaningful contribution to the security of the EU's supply of lithium and to the achievements of the 2030 CRMA benchmarks. It will reduce the EU's dependency on external sources of lithium, mitigating risks associated with geopolitical tensions and supply chain disruptions. O European Union, 2025

name: La Parrilla Mine (P6 Metals)
fs_description: La Parrilla Mine project is an integrated tungsten extraction and processing project in southwest Spain. It is aimed at reopening an existing tungsten open pit mine connected to an already constructed processing plant. The mine is expected to be back in full production during 2026 with a life of mine of 18 years. The mine is situated on relatively flat ground with sufficient real-estate for all required infrastructure; existing plant, site offces, tailings ponds, access roads.
fs_benefit: La Parrilla Mine project would make a meaningful contribution to the security of the EU's supply of tungsten, contributing to the achievements of the 2030 CRMA benchmarks. The mine is the largest tungsten mine worldwide, outside of China, with a vain ore type mineralization. According to the project promoter, the project would produce 30 % of the current internal EU production of tungsten. The project promoter has the intention to sell their products to a diversified customer base with offtake contracts and preliminary end-users that have been already identified in the EU. name: Mining project EL MOTO
fs_description: El Moto tungsten project is an extraction project located in Abenåjar, province of Ciudad Real (Spain). fs_description: Aguablanca is an "Extraction Project" located in the Extremadura Region, Spain. Mined ore will be processed in the existing 5,000 tpd processing plant by three-stage crushing followed by conventional grinding and product slurry conditioning. Processing of the conditioned slurry product will be followed by a conventional sulfide flotation system to produce a bulk sulfide concentrate for the recovery of the above mentioned raw materials. fs_description: CaledoNi is an industrial modernisation project with the objective of increasing the production of nickel with a better environmental impact. Once commissioned, the Doniambo site is expected to reduce diffuse dust emissions by 30% and canalised dust emissions by 14%.
fs_benefit: Caledonia The intended processing of nickel will contribute to the security of supply of critical raw materials in the EU, guarantee a source diversification and reduce the risks associated with external suppliers of this material. The project will enable increased feed into potential matte production for processing battery-grade nickel. name: Integrated Dumont Nickel Project
fs_benefit_heading: Benefit for the EU and Canada
fs_description: The Integrated Dumont Nickel Project is a nickel and cobalt sulphide advanced stage development project located in the Abitibi region of Quebec, Canada. Construction for the project is expected to begin in 2026. Once in production, expected to be in the first quarter of 2029, Dumont will produce 42,000 tonnes of nickel annually which is sufficient for approximately 840,000 EV batteries yearly. The project has a planned life of mine of 29 years. The project was assessed as having a substantially lower carbon footprint compared to other producers.
fs_benefit: The Integrated Dumont Nickel Project will significantly contribute to the EU's diversified of supply for nickel and cobalt. The promoter already committed 40% of production to an EU automotive company and further agreements are under negotiation. The project will contribute to sustainable raw material supply chains through the use of hydroelectric power and lowcarbon technologies. The promoter has also pursued proactive engagement with Indigenous groups, through an Impact Benefit Agreement, which supports employment, training, and business opportunities. The Jadar Project would be developed as an underground mine and processing operation.

name: Kobaloni Energy Zambia Ltd
fs_benefit_heading: Benefit for EU and third country
fs_description: The Kobaloni Energy Zambia project is a processing project located in Zambia. The project will source power from hydro-power sources and process cobalt at the site of extraction. The project has already been designated as a Minerals Security Partnership project.
fs_benefit: The Kobaloni cobalt project would have the potential to contribute significantly to the EU's 2030 target for diversifying critical raw material sourcing, given that it would reduce the EU reliance on a single third country that currently refines 95% of the world's cobalt for electric vehicles. The project is considered to be aligned with the EU's development cooperation and foreign policy objectives. It would benefit both the local and regional mineral value chains, increasing the value of processed materials leaving Africa, creating several hundred of jobs and investment in local suppliers, while boosting Zambia's export sector and enhancing its reputation as reliable source for essential materials in the electric vehicle battery supply chain. fs_description: The Tungsten West project is an extraction project by Tungsten West PLC located near Plymouth in South Devon, United Kingdom. The project aims to restore the historic Hemerdon mining and mineral processing operations to produce concentrates of the strategic raw material tungsten. Tungsten is essential in strategic technologies due to its strength and durability, making it ideal for applications in the aerospace and defence sector. Drawing from established insights gained from previous mining operations, the project incorporates advanced mineral processing techniques to enhance efficiency and output.
fs_benefit: United Kingdom The Tungsten West project aims to establish a secure tungsten supply chain for the United Kingdom and the EU, supporting the EU's goal of a diversified, resilient supply network crucial for strategic sectors like aerospace and defence. It seeks to boost the local economy by generating numerous direct and indirect jobs, focusing on revitalizing economically challenged areas in the United Kingdom and improving community well-being. Through local supplier partnerships and proactive community dialogue, the project contributes to sustainable development and enhances regional economic growth. O European Union, 2025

fs_description: The Zandkopsdrift project is an integrated extraction and processing project located in South Africa that will produce two Strategic Raw Materials magnet rare earths and battery grade manganese. The mining operations are fully permitted with sufficient reserves to support a 45year mine life. The production of two high value Strategic Raw Materials from a single integrated operation is expected to result in low production costs for both materials. A DFS is under way and scheduled for completion in 2027, with first production targeted for 2029.
fs_benefit: Africa The Zandkopsdrift project will contribute significantly to the EU's security of supply and reduce its reliance on imports in respect of magnet RES and battery grade manganese. By producing materials essential for strategic technologies, such as EVs, wind turbines and lithium-ion batteries, it will help to reduce the EU's vulnerability to supply disruptions for these Strategic Raw Materials. The project will have a positive impact in South Africa through a community trust that holds a 21% interest in the project, direct and indirect jobs that will be created, and infrastructure upgrades, thus aligning with the EU's commitment to sustainable development and mineral beneficiation in Africa.
